children: on Tuesday said it is expanding its treadmill lineup with three new models, including its first folding treadmill, while adding AI-powered coaching features aimed at runners, walkers, and hikers.

The company said Tuesday that the Peloton Tread Flex, Tread Vision, and Tread+ Vision will launch in Canada on October 1, with the Tread Flex starting at C$2,995. The Tread Flex will be available in Peloton’s other markets in spring 2027, while the Tread Vision will launch across all Peloton
markets on October 1, starting at C$4,395 in Canada. The Tread+ Vision will also launch in Canada on October 1 at C$8,395.

The Tread Flex folds to reduce its footprint by nearly 50%, while Tread Vision adds a movement-tracking camera that provides post-run form insights. The Tread+ Vision includes the same camera technology and adds a Sled Mode feature with up to 300 pounds of resistance.

is also expanding its Peloton IQ software with features including Run Analysis, which evaluates cadence, vertical oscillation, and stride length; personalized pace targets; heart-rate-zone workouts; and ReRuns, which lets members sync inclines from outdoor routes.
The company also announced a partnership with wearable-device maker WHOOP, allowing users to connect their Peloton
and WHOOP accounts and sync workout data between the platforms.
CEO Peter Stern said the product expansion is intended to broaden the company's reach in the at-home treadmill market.
Shares were up about 4% in the premarket trading on Tuesday.

title: Peloton expands treadmill lineup with folding model, AI features
